subject: ClearBank — private connectivity decision details and egress checklist
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Rao <asha.rao@clearbank.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@clearbank.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-21T09:18:00-05:00
Subject: ClearBank post-demo — connectivity model recap + ask

Hi Asha / Tom — great to meet you earlier. Recap of the options we discussed and the pieces we need to lock down to select Private VPC (PrivateLink) vs VPC Peering vs Dedicated capacity: 

Summary of customer goals
- Primary: keep all inference traffic inside ClearBank-owned VPCs and meet SOC2/data residency constraints.
- Secondary: minimize egress cost exposure and avoid customer-managed public IPs for our serving endpoints.

Options we reviewed
1) Hosted API (fastest) — requires customer allowlist/privatelink to restrict access; best for quick start but still routes through Redwood-managed network.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) — logical isolation, Redwood-owned endpoints; needs peering or privatelink to avoid public egress.
3) Private VPC (VPC endpoint in your account / on-prem tunnel) — full network isolation, customer owns TLS termination and outbound NAT.

Critical network decisions for Private VPC path (what we need from NetOps)
- Preferred connectivity: PrivateLink endpoint or VPC Peering? If PrivateLink, we need the target NLB subnet range to allow inbound. If Peering, we need a shared route table plan and confirmation of transitive routing policy.
- Egress model: will you accept Redwood-managed egress IPs (we can dedicate a small set for your tenant) or must all outbound go through your NAT (transit gateway / proxy)?
- Allowlist: please confirm CIDR(s) and FQDNs you want on the allowlist. We provided a starter CSV (attached) — please annotate which CIDRs are acceptable.
- TLS / certs: who will terminate TLS? If ClearBank, provide cert chain or ACME plan.
- KMS / key custody: any requirement for customer-managed keys for logs or attachments?

Next steps / asks by EOD Tue (2027-11-23)
- Asha / NetOps: confirm preferred connectivity type and paste allowlist CIDRs into the attached CSV.
- Tom: share contact for the transit gateway owner if outbound must egress through your NAT.
- Jordan / Ben (cc): we'll prepare a network diagram and a short checklist for onboarding once you confirm the above.

Attachments: privatenet-egress-table.csv (starter CIDR list), clearbank-malp-qs.pdf (security questionnaire answers we drafted)

Thanks — happy to jump back on a 30-min call to walk the network team through this.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@clearbank.com>

Cc: netops@clearbank.com, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-21T11:02:00-05:00
Subject: Re: ClearBank post-demo — connectivity model recap + ask

Hannah — thanks for the clear notes. A few clarifications from NetOps after our infra sync: 

1) Preferred connectivity: PrivateLink is our default for third-party managed endpoints (no cross-account peering unless absolutely necessary). PrivateLink avoids exposing peered route tables to other accounts.

2) Egress: ClearBank policy prefers customer-managed egress for auditability. We will not allow Redwood to egress directly to the internet from within our VPC. That means traffic from the Redwood endpoint must traverse our NAT/proxy (Transit Gateway).

3) Allowlist: I updated the attached CSV with our internal NAT egress IP block (10.200.12.0/24) and the Transit Gateway endpoint IPs. See the attached privatenet-egress-table.csv.

4) TLS: We plan to terminate TLS at our NLB. We'll need a short runbook from Redwood on the expected SNI and certificate chain upload process.

5) KMS: We will want customer-managed keys for S3 logs; I'll send KMS contact separately.

Action items on our side:
- I'll loop in Sara (transit-gateway-owner) and ask her to review the flow and confirm routing.
- We'll schedule a 30-min setup call next week for the NetOps integration. Suggested slots: Wed 11/24 10–12 or Thu 11/25 14–16 (ET).

Tom
Tom Ellis | Senior Network Engineer, ClearBank
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@clearbank.com>, Asha Rao <asha.rao@clearbank.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Peter Nguyen <peter.consultant@infra-partners.com>
Date: 2027-11-21T14:30:00-05:00
Subject: Re: ClearBank post-demo — connectivity model recap + ask

Tom / Asha — appreciate the fast turnaround. A few technical clarifications and what we'll bring to the setup call: 

- PrivateLink + Customer egress via Transit Gateway is a supported pattern for Redwood. Implementation notes:
  * We'll provision a cross-account NLB in the Redwood control plane that fronts the model endpoints and advertise a PrivateLink service for you to create the endpoint in your VPC.
  * Because you require customer-managed egress, traffic arriving at your VPC via the interface endpoint will be routed to your NLB and then egress through your NAT/TGW. That means responses to the inference request will still traverse your egress path — which aligns with your audit requirement.
  * We will need one /28 (or larger) subnet for the interface endpoint ENIs in the AZs you want to use. The attached CSV shows a suggested allocation; confirm which AZs and subnets are preferred.

- IP allowlist alternative: if you decide to accept Redwood-managed egress for a short pilot, we can allocate a stable set of public egress IPs and lock them per-tenant for allowlisting, which speeds onboarding. But we understand that is not your preference long-term.

- Certificate exchange: For TLS termination at your NLB, you'll need to share the public key fingerprint (SHA256) so we can validate the endpoint certificate during mutual TLS checks. If you prefer mutual TLS, let us know and we'll provide the CA bundle and cert rotation expectations.

What we'll prepare for the setup call:
- Simple network diagram showing PrivateLink -> your NLB -> TGW -> NAT flow
- Step-by-step PrivateLink endpoint creation guide and minimal Route53/hostname guidance if you want a CNAME in your internal DNS
- ACL/security group suggestions for the interface endpoint and NLB 

Proposed times: Wed 11/24 10:30–11:00 ET (tight), Thu 11/25 14:00–14:45 ET (preferred). Hannah / Ben to confirm on Redwood side.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai

- I've uploaded the annotated CSV with the AZ/subnet choices and TGW attachment IDs. See privatenet-egress-table.csv.
- Proposed pilot: one environment (staging) first, then production after validation. Staging timeline: aim for setup week of Dec 6.
- On the setup call please have the PrivateLink service name, expected port (443), and the NLB subnet sizing recommendation. Also include a short checklist for our security team showing where to find logs and what will be stored in Redwood-managed S3.

Tom / NetOps: Sara will pick a time on Wed 11/24 10:30 ET that works for the TGW team.
